Analysis by Richard Cowan

Posted August 17, 2007

 

Last week I complained that the anti-war Left was ignoring the damage that the drug war is doing to both our own civil liberties and the poor people in Latin America, especially Mexico.

See

Sicko and The Return of MarijuanaNews.com. The Failure of the Left to Address the Drug War. By Richard Cowan.   

This was not a new theme for readers of MarijuanaNews

See

From 2003

Now, How the Narks Created Smack in Mexico. Replacing Marijuana With Poppies. The Iron Law of Prohibition Keeps Working, But The Media Dont

and

From 2005

Mexico, the Drugwar and the US National Interest: Never Mind Iraq; We Need To Pay Attention to What We Are Doing to Our Southern Neighbor.



It is about to get more difficult for anyone to ignore.

 

Next week, President Bush and President Felipe Calderón of Mexico will be the guests of Canadian Prime Minister Stephen Harper at a summit in Quebec. If the details can be worked out in time, it is expected that a new Plan Mexico will be announced that would provide Mexico with hundreds of millions of dollars in laid as much as $1.2 billion over three years to help Calderon further militarize law enforcement in Mexico.

 

Calderon very narrowly defeated the leftist mayor of Mexico City in the 2006 Presidential election. With only a very limited mandate and much popular skepticism Calderon used the fear caused by an increase in drug war violence to win popular support.

 

The turf wars between gangs were spilling over into tourist areas and threatening Mexico's small but important upper middle class. (The wealthiest Mexicans have long lived with high levels of security.) Border towns were becoming literally lawless.

From 2006 See

Updates About Kubby, Overgrow.com, Mexico. When A Mexican City Becomes More Dangerous Than Washington, DC

So Calderon brought in the military to oversee and even replace the notoriously corrupt Mexican police. However, so far, it has been more successful politically than militarily. Surprise!

 

There are now reports of corruption in the military and accusations of abuses by troops.

 

These accusations echo those made in Colombia over the last six years since Plan Colombia got under way. (Actually, it began under President Clinton who ignored US law prohibiting drug war aid to the military in countries where the military violated human rights.) 

See

Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews World Report for May 16, 2005 Chaos on Mexican Border, Even Worse in Colombia; Ever More Bonkers in Britain; A Hanging in Singapore and Faint Hope in Australia.

And

DEAland Collaborates With Colombia Cartels To Bring Cocaine And Violence To The Caribbean. Island Growers Caught In The Middle.



Colombia has received more than $5 Billion in drug war aid from the US since 2000, more than any other country outside the Middle East and Afghanistan. (Of course, Afghanistan is one more place where the drug war has taken precedence over the national interest.)

See

Remembrance and Ignorance: In Afghan fields the poppies grow...  



We have also paid for bribes to demobilize rightwing paramilitary gangs. Unfortunately, as the AP reported earlier this week, New criminal gangs are emerging in areas once controlled by paramilitary groups, undermining a peace process under which 31,000 right-wing fighters have demobilized...

 

The armed gangs, dedicated mainly to drug trafficking and extortion, have as many as 5,000 members, 17 percent of which are believed to be rearmed paramilitaries who renounced violence under a 2003 peace accord, according to the report released by the Commission of Reparation and Reconciliation. 34 independent bands had surfaced in 200 municipalities across the country.

 

T'was a great victory.

See
US To Increase Support For Colombian Army; Those Who Do Not Learn From History

and

The "Vietnamization" of the Drug War; US Narco-Imperialism Goes In Search of Enemies
The Quagmire of Tomorrow
and links

 

Sadly, Mexico and Colombia really do seem like victories when compared with poor Guatemala. In 2005, a great article in the Texas Monthly reported, For decades, successive U.S. administrations have tried and failed to train effective Guatemalan police, while saying little or nothing about the known criminal activities of the Guatemalan military.

 

The drug gangs are also trying to influence the presidential campaign under way there. Earlier this month the New York Times reported, Guatemala provides an increasingly important transit point, American officials say, as traffickers take advantage of the country's dire poverty and lawlessness.

 

With plenty of money to spend, drug dealers finance as many campaigns as they can and put forward candidates who are on the take.  Resistance is met with gunfire.

Guatemala borders the Mexican state of Chiapas, which has been the scene of a leftist rebellion by the Zapatistas, but that is not the only political unrest in the country. The city of Oaxaca has also been the wracked by violent political protests, sparked by the corruption and incompetence of the state governor. So, we should recognize that while the political problems in Mexico are not (yet) as severe as those in Colombia  much less Guatemala  the use of the military for law enforcement can create real political problems.

 

So, now we are going to duplicate our success with the military in Guatemala and Iraq and Colombia in Mexico  with only a billion or so. Will anyone notice?

 

One would hope that the Democrats would at least raise some relevant questions, but, unfortunately, the biggest backers of Plan Mexico are Mexican American Democrats in the House, Rep. Henry Cuellar of Laredo and Rep. Rep.  Silvestre Reyes of El Paso. Both are drug warriors who even voted against restricting DEA attacks on medical marijuana dispensaries in states with medical marijuana laws. Lock my people up!!??

 

Ironically, it may be the sensitivity of Mexican nationalism i. e. distrust of gringos that scuttles this deal. Please, please, pretty please, take our money... is not something that will go over too well in Washington these days.

 

Lou Dobbs will be even more red in the face than usual. Blame Canada is a song from the South Park movie and heretofore the favorite of our beloved Drug Czar.

See

Bush Should Have John Comical Ali Walters Explain The Iraq War, Then The Media Would Never Ask Any Embarrassing Questions. Doctrine Of Drug Czar Infallibility? Blame Canada, Again.



However, Blame Mexico is the new anthem of the prohibitionists. That will not translate well.

From 2006, See

Lou Dobbs and the Second Mexican War. Has It Already Begun? Counting the Costs of the Drugwar.

 

Whatever the fate of Plan Mexico, we will continue to sacrifice our national interest and Mexican stability which should be among our highest national priorities to the Drug War.

Mexico can and should act unilaterally to legalize cannabis, but it will not be able to free itself of the transit traffic in heroin and cocaine, or the problems associated with manufacturing meth, which has now been moved there, without DEAland leading the way.

 

Obviously, that is not going to happen under Bush, nor is Calderon, a social conservative, likely to place Mexico's well-being ahead of the prohibitionist ideology.

Any decline in the US economy, accompanied by increased enforcement of immigration laws, will put pressure on Mexico's economy and social stability. Will the Drug War then be allowed onto the Public Agenda? 

 

"When the day comes that it is time to adopt the alternative of lifting punishment for consumption of drugs, it would have to come all over the world. Humanity some day will see that it is best in that sense." Former Mexican President Vicente Fox
